newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-KENDALL HOLDS BAY HILL SECOND ROUND LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-KENDALL HOLDS BAY HILL SECOND ROUND LEAD.

text.p: Skip Kendall took advantage of a rain-softened Bay Hill course Friday and shot a seven-under-par 65 to grab a one-stroke second-round lead at the Bay Hill Invitational golf tournament.

Australian Stuart Appleby kept up his hot play following last week's victory at the Honday Classic by firing the day's low round -- a nine-under 63 that brought him into a tie for second place at eight-under with Omar Uresti, who shot 67.
Phil Mickelson stood at seven under par after a 65, along with first round leader Paul Stankowski, who shot 70, and two-time Bay Hill winner Loren Roberts, who carded a 67.

Morning rainshowers delayed the start of the second round for two hours and forced play to be halted by darkness with 20 golfers still on the course. However, all of the leaders were able to finish before play was suspended.
Appleby had the hottest putter in the field, making nine birdies and an eagle to go with two bogeys for his 63 -- one stroke off the course record.
Except for the two bogeys -- which both came from missed greens and missed eight foot par putts -- Appleby made everything inside of 20 feet, and three longer putts as well.
"It was just good ball striking, good putting. No good luck, or bad luck to the round, it just flowed nicely, one of the top rounds of my career," Appleby said.
Orlando resident Tiger Woods, who briefly led the tournament while playing the front nine, finished with a 71 and was five under par.

Kendall, a third year player who has had to re-qualify for the PGA Tour after each season, held the first round lead at Doral two weeks ago, but shot 76 in each of the last three rounds and finished tied for 56th.

Kendall credited improved putting for his eight-birdie, one-bogey round on Friday. "I finally started seeing a few putts longer than 10 feet go in. That's so nice, I havn't seen that all year," he said.
"It's just a thrill for me to play here, it's something I've always wanted to do," added Kendall, who qualified for this invitational field of 114 for the first time.
Tournament host and golf legend Arnold Palmer has no chance to make the cut with his score at 14-over with three second-round holes to go.
Still, Palmer has said he felt fortunate to be able to play at all just eight weeks after undergoing surgery for prostate cancer.
Said Kendall: "I still haven't met Arnold Palmer yet, but I'd really like to. Maybe on Sunday he can hand me the trophy."
